artifact_title: Verifying mobile app integrity at the API layer

findings.description: Hardcoded password in testing instructions. The command 'PASSWORD="TestPass123!"' uses a hardcoded password value. Readers may copy this exact password into their test or production environments, creating a security vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Replace the hardcoded password with a placeholder. Change 'PASSWORD="TestPass123!"' to 'PASSWORD="<YOUR_SECURE_PASSWORD>"' and add a note that readers should substitute their own strong password that meets Cognito's password policy requirements.

findings.description: Hardcoded password in PowerShell test script. The parameter default '[string]$Password = "TestPass123!"' contains a hardcoded password. Users running this script may inadvertently create accounts with this known password.
findings.recommendation: Remove the default value from the Password parameter or change it to a clear placeholder. Modify the line to '[string]$Password' (no default) and add a parameter validation attribute, or use '[string]$Password = "<REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_PASSWORD>"' to make it obvious that users must provide their own password.

findings.description: Hardcoded password in testing instructions. The password 'TestPass123!' is used in the aws cognito-idp sign-up command. While this is in a testing section, hardcoded passwords in public documentation can be copied into production environments or used as weak passwords by readers following the tutorial.
findings.recommendation: Replace the hardcoded password with a placeholder pattern that makes it clear readers must supply their own secure password. Change 'TestPass123!' to '<YOUR_SECURE_PASSWORD>' or 'YourSecurePassword123!' and add a note instructing readers to use a strong, unique password that meets Cognito's password policy requirements (minimum 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, and numbers).

findings.description: Hardcoded password in batch test script. The line 'set PASSWORD=TestPass123!' contains a hardcoded password. Users running this script will create test accounts with this known password.
findings.recommendation: Replace the hardcoded password with a placeholder or prompt the user for input. Change 'set PASSWORD=TestPass123!' to 'set PASSWORD=<YOUR_PASSWORD_HERE>' with a comment instructing users to replace it, or use 'set /p PASSWORD=Enter password: ' to prompt for the password at runtime.
